scope: CAD-derived subsystem proposals; native source geometry is present, but this software preview grants no visual or physical approval. Fill in per-subsystem Constants for the installed robot. Selected behavior recipes are listed; other classes provide named capability APIs. No electrical configuration, physical operation or robot-ready approval verified.

files.content:
# Generated FTC robot code

Plain FTC SDK v12 Java. No extra libraries.

- config: one Constants class per mechanism with hardware-map labels, directions and powers/positions.
- hardware/subsystems: one class per mechanism. Construct it with the HardwareMap and call its named actions.
- robots/Robot.java: builds every subsystem. Use `new Robot(hardwareMap)` in your OpMode and call `stop()` when done.

Copy src/main/java into TeamCode, then edit the Constants files so labels match your robot configuration and the powers, velocities and servo positions match your robot. The defaults are starting points, not tuned values.

## Mechanisms

- Drivetrain: hardware/subsystems/Drivetrain.java
- Intake: hardware/subsystems/Intake.java
- Feeder: hardware/subsystems/Feeder.java
- Pollen pusher: hardware/subsystems/PollenPusher.java
- Shooter: hardware/subsystems/Shooter.java

review.summary: Source preview emits config Constants and hardware subsystems for Drivetrain, Intake, Feeder, PollenPusher and Shooter with HardwareMap constructors, named actions and Robot composition with stop(). Types and control modes match the planned outputs: tank drivetrain on two DcMotorEx, intake motor power start/clear, feeder CRServo feed/reverse, pollen pusher Servo extend/retract endpoints, shooter DcMotorEx velocity spinUp/isAtSpeed. No compile/API defects, no constructor powering, no missing subsystem construction in Robot.stop(). Constants are editable starting points.

findings.message: Feeder is implemented as CRServo with power feed/reverse. Implementation plan lists servoPower and optional servoPosition capability; positional setActuatorPosition is not emitted, which is acceptable for a continuous servo but limits positional use if required.

Shooter.stop() sets power to zero while motor is in RUN_USING_ENCODER and previously driven with setVelocity. Stopping velocity explicitly is safer; current stop still halts output but does not clear velocity target.
Drive scaling uses power = drivePower / max(1,|forward|+|turn|). Normalization is functional but non-standard; verify robot forward mapping and direction signs match physical wiring.

compilation.scope: Official FTC SDK v12.0; Android API 30 bootstrap; Java 8; compile only

behaviors.name: Drivetrain
requiredConfiguration: Explicit runtime assignment of every source motor to left or right; at least one on each side
Configured motor directions and independent output ownership
Confirmed robot forward/up frame; drive() is robot-centric
No side mapping, wiring, odometry or field-centric conversion is inferred

behaviors.name: Intake
requiredConfiguration: Explicitly configured motor directions and independent output ownership
Independently selected job and reversing powers for every motor; open-loop power is not a measured speed or readiness signal
No automatic sensing or jam recovery is claimed without an installed input and policy

behaviors.name: Feeder
requiredConfiguration: Explicitly established continuous-servo adapters before named powered actions
Selected independent forward/reverse powers and configured directions for every servo
Positional capability remains separately guarded where mode is unknown; no timed gate or measured endpoints are inferred

behaviors.name: Pollen pusher
requiredConfiguration: Explicit positional servo mode for each output
Measured extended/retracted endpoints for every servo
stop() holds positional servos; it does not infer a safe retract policy

behaviors.name: Shooter
requiredConfiguration: Actual encoder feedback on every flywheel motor
Measured encoder ticks per output revolution for each wheel
Configured velocity PIDF, directions and independent ownership
Selected maximum RPM, readiness tolerance, dwell and sample freshness
Monotonic seconds and update() on every robot loop
